claims.hypothesis: Fragments in molecular shells of compact H II regions differ from fragments elsewhere in the same clump
claims.experiment: Classify 164 H13CO+ fragments as N or F and compare sigma, sigma_NT, mass, Sigma, n_H2 and R_vir with K-S tests
claims.result: N fragments have larger sigma, mass and surface density (Sigma ~1 g cm-2 vs ~0.4 lower; M ~25 vs ~10 Msun; sigma ~0.7 vs ~0.5 km/s); no clear difference in R_vir
claims.finding: Shells swept up by early H II regions host more massive, denser, more turbulent fragments that may favour higher-mass star formation

evidence.quote: These gas fragments, strongly affected by the H II region, have a higher surface density, mass, and turbulence than those outside the shells but within the same pc-scale natal clump.
mass ($M\sim25$ $\rm M_\odot$, $\sim15$ $\rm M_\odot$ larger)

claims.hypothesis: The fragments formed by fragmentation (collect and collapse) of the swept-up shell
claims.experiment: Compare Whitworth1994 t_frag, r_frag, M_frag, D_frag with H II region age, size and observed fragments, with two n_ini cases
claims.result: t_frag ~0.5-0.7 Myr and r_frag ~0.8 pc exceed the H II region age (>~0.3 Myr) and radius (~0.2 pc); M_frag and D_frag are much larger than observed
claims.finding: Shell fragmentation is unlikely to have produced the fragments in these early H II regions

evidence.quote: fragmentation of the swept-up shell is unlikely to occur in these early H II regions
which is against the shell fragmentation origin of fragments

claims.hypothesis: The fragments are pre-existing, formed by Jeans fragmentation of the natal clump, and swept into the shell
claims.experiment: Compare MST separations with Jeans lengths; ATPCF of fragments around H II regions; velocity difference between fragments and H II region
claims.result: Most separations similar to or shorter than L_Jeans; ATPCF peaks near the H II region edge; N fragments show larger velocity dispersion about the H II region velocity
claims.finding: Fragments probably formed by Jeans fragmentation before the shell swept them up, and their distribution and kinematics were regulated by expansion and photoevaporation

evidence.quote: We propose that the appearance of gas fragments in these shells is probably the result of sweeping up pre-existing fragments into the molecular shell that has not yet fragmented.
suggesting that fragments in shells can be explained as a result of clump-to-fragment Jeans fragmentation predominant by thermal motions

claims.hypothesis: Stellar winds contribute significantly to the dynamics and fragmentation of the shells
claims.experiment: Compute the Geen2020 C_w factor for two natal cloud cases and wind-driven fragmentation times
claims.finding: Winds are non-negligible at the HC stage but unimportant at the compact stage

evidence.quote: we have $C_{\rm w}$ of 0.4 and 0.08 for these two cases
stellar winds on the dynamics of the early compact H II regions are generally unimportant

claims.hypothesis: N fragments grow faster in mass than F fragments
claims.experiment: Compare fragment mass with H II region size and fragment-to-clump mass ratio
claims.result: Positive correlation of mass with H II size for both types; difference not significant, distance bias possible
claims.finding: Cannot confirm or reject a higher accretion rate for N fragments

evidence.quote: Therefore, we cannot confirm or reject the scenario in which N fragments have a higher mass accretion rate from our limited observations

referee_caveats_inferred: Fragment masses depend on a single uniform H13CO+ abundance (3.6e-11) and Tex = clump Tdust, with N/F temperature offsets of +/-5 K assumed, so the N vs F mass difference is not independent of those choices
Dynamical age and n_ini use present-day clump densities and the classical expansion law, so t_frag versus age comparison is order-of-magnitude
Conclusions rest on nine regions at different distances (1.8-6.2 kpc) with natural-weighted ~2 arcsec beam, so resolution and sensitivity bias fragment extraction
Pre-existing fragment scenario is inferred, not directly tested; no direct kinematic or temperature measurement of the shell
K-S test details and multiple-comparison handling are not given
